blocks.text: Why freight broker carrier performance tracking falls apart

Most brokerages treat carrier performance as a reactive chore. You only notice a problem when a load is late or an invoice is wrong. This happens because your data is fragmented. Your carrier emails are in Gmail, your load details are in a TMS, and your performance notes are likely in a separate Google Sheet. When you have to toggle between three apps to verify a carrier, you stop tracking performance and start just chasing fires.
The hidden costs of manual tracking

Poor tracking is a direct hit to your bottom line. Every time you manually reconcile a carrier invoice against a rate confirmation, you spend valuable time. If you miscalculate a payment, the cost of a stop payment request is often $20. Multiply that by even a small percentage of your annual loads, and you are looking at significant financial loss. Worse, your team spends hours on these tasks instead of finding new capacity.

items: Consolidate your data into a single TMS. If your TMS is web-based, ensure it runs smoothly in Safari or Chrome on your Mac.
Create a simple carrier scorecard. Track only three things: On-Time Delivery rate, Tender Acceptance, and Invoice Accuracy.
Automate your carrier vetting. Use tools that pull real-time FMCSA safety data to verify compliance before you even book the load.
Schedule a 30-minute quarterly review. Use your data to show carriers exactly where they are succeeding and where they are failing.

blocks.text: If you use Google Sheets to track performance, use the Data > Sort Range feature to quickly identify your top and bottom carriers by margin or OTD rate.

faq.question: Can I use legacy Windows TMS software on my Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, but you may need virtualization software like Parallels or Citrix to run those older applications on macOS.

faq.question: What is the most important metric to track?
faq.answer: On-Time Delivery (OTD) rate is generally considered the most critical for maintaining shipper trust, followed closely by margin per load.

faq.question: How often should I review carrier performance?
faq.answer: A quarterly review is usually enough to drive behavior change without overwhelming your staff or your carrier partners.
